name: Sit to stand from a chair
steps: Sit near the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat, hip-width apart.
Lean forward a little and push through your feet to stand.
Stand tall for a moment, then sit down slowly.
Use your hands on the chair arms or your knees if you need to.

name: Slow chair stand
steps: Sit at the front of a sturdy chair.
Stand up slowly.
Sit back down, taking 3 slow counts to lower.

name: Heel raises holding a counter
steps: Stand behind a chair or at a counter, both hands on it.
Rise up onto your toes slowly.
Lower your heels slowly.
Keep your knees soft, not locked.
stopIf: Your calf cramps and does not ease

video.title: Toe Stand Strength Exercise for Older Adults

name: Toe raises holding a counter
steps: Stand with both hands on a counter or chair back.
Lift the front of your feet, heels stay down.
Lower slowly.

name: Seated march
steps: Sit tall near the front of a chair.
Lift one knee, then lower it.
Switch legs, like slow walking in place.
Breathe normally.
stopIf: You cannot talk while you do it

name: Wall push-up
steps: Face a wall, an arm's length away, hands on the wall at shoulder height.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall.
Push back to straight arms, slowly.
Keep your back straight.

video.title: Wall Pushups Strength Exercise for Older Adults

name: Seated knee straightening
steps: Sit tall in a chair.
Slowly straighten one knee until your leg is level.
Lower it slowly. Do the other leg.
Breathe out as you lift.

name: Seated leg lift with a hold
steps: Sit tall in a chair.
Straighten one knee and hold it level for 5 slow counts.
Lower and switch legs.
Keep breathing; do not hold your breath.

name: Seated arm raises
steps: Sit tall, arms by your sides. Hold a small water bottle if you like.
Lift both arms to the front, up to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
Breathe out as you lift.

name: Bottle curls
steps: Sit tall holding a small water bottle in each hand.
Bend your elbows to bring the bottles to your shoulders.
Lower slowly.

name: Standing leg out to the side
steps: Stand tall holding a counter or chair back.
Slowly lift one leg out to the side, a small way.
Lower it. Do the other leg.
Keep your toes pointing forward.

video.title: Side Leg Raise - Strength Training Exercise for Older Adults

name: Hip bridge on the bed
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
Press your feet down and lift your hips a little.
Lower slowly.
Breathe out as you lift.

name: March in place near a chair
steps: Stand tall next to a sturdy chair, one hand on it.
Lift one knee, then the other, at an easy pace.
Swing your free arm.
Slow down if you get out of breath.
stopIf: You cannot talk while you do it

name: Foot in front of foot, holding a chair
tl: Isang paa sa harap ng isa
steps: Stand next to a sturdy chair and hold it.
Place one foot directly in front of the other, heel touching toes.
Stay for up to 30 seconds. Switch feet.
Keep breathing.
stopIf: You lose your balance and need to grab the chair

name: Stand on one foot holding a counter
steps: Hold a counter with both hands.
Lift one foot a little off the floor.
Stay for up to 20 seconds, then switch.
Use one hand only when you feel steady.

video.title: Stand on One Foot Balance Exercise for Older Adults

name: Weight shift side to side
steps: Stand holding a counter, feet hip-width apart.
Slowly shift your weight onto your right foot.
Slowly shift to your left foot.
Keep your hips level.

name: Heel-to-toe steps along a counter
steps: Stand at the end of a counter, one hand on it.
Step forward, placing your heel just in front of the other toes.
Walk along the counter like this.
Turn around and come back.

video.title: Heel-to-Toe Walk Balance Exercise for Older Adults

name: Seated reach to the side
steps: Sit tall in a sturdy chair, feet flat.
Reach one arm out to the side, a small way.
Return to the middle. Switch sides.
Keep your hips on the seat.

name: Ankle circles
steps: Sit in a chair and lift one foot a little.
Draw slow circles with your toes, 5 each way.
Switch feet.

name: Seated hamstring stretch
steps: Sit at the front edge of a chair.
Straighten one leg, heel on the floor, toes up.
Sit tall and lean forward a little from the hip until you feel a gentle pull.
Stay for 20 seconds, breathing normally. Switch legs.

video.title: Back Of Leg Stretch for Older Adults

name: Shoulder rolls
steps: Sit tall with arms relaxed.
Roll your shoulders up, back and down in a slow circle, 5 times.
Roll them the other way, 5 times.

name: Gentle neck turns
steps: Sit tall and look straight ahead.
Slowly turn your head to the right as far as is comfortable.
Come back to the middle, then turn left.
Do not tip your head back.
stopIf: Pain or tingling in your arms

name: Hand and wrist stretch
steps: Hold one arm out in front, palm up.
With the other hand, gently bend the fingers down toward the floor.
Stay 10 seconds. Switch hands.
Open and close your fists 10 times.

name: Calf stretch at a wall
steps: Stand facing a wall, hands on it.
Step one foot back, heel down.
Bend the front knee a little until you feel a gentle pull in the back leg.
Stay for 20 seconds. Switch.

name: Seated chest opener
steps: Sit tall at the front of the chair.
Hold the chair back behind you, or rest your hands on your hips.
Gently lift your chest and breathe in.
Breathe out and relax.

name: Easy 5-minute walk
steps: Choose a flat, even place, indoors or in the shade.
Walk at a pace where you can still talk.
Wear shoes that fit and grip.
Stop and sit if you need a rest.
stopIf: You cannot talk while you do it

name: Easy 10-minute walk
steps: Choose a flat, even place.
Walk at a pace where you can still talk.
Bring water if it is warm.
Stop and sit if you need a rest.
stopIf: You cannot talk while you do it

name: Indoor walk back and forth
steps: Pick a clear path at home with a wall or furniture to touch.
Walk to the end and back.
Keep a steady, easy pace.
Sit down if you feel tired.
stopIf: You cannot talk while you do it

name: Slow breathing
steps: Sit comfortably with your back supported.
Breathe in through your nose for about 4 counts.
Breathe out gently through your mouth for about 6 counts.
Keep going for 2 minutes. Never hold your breath.

name: Belly breathing
steps: Sit back and rest one hand on your belly.
Breathe in slowly so your belly rises.
Breathe out slowly so it falls.
Repeat for 2 minutes.

name: Pursed-lip breathing
steps: Sit comfortably.
Breathe in through your nose for 2 counts.
Purse your lips like blowing out a candle and breathe out slowly for 4 counts.
Repeat for 2 minutes.

name: Neck side tilt
steps: Sit tall with your shoulders loose and relaxed.
Slowly tip your right ear toward your right shoulder. Do not lift the shoulder.
Stop where you feel a gentle stretch and breathe out once.
Come back to the middle, then do the other side.
stopIf: Tingling, numbness or pain that shoots down an arm or leg
Pain that gets worse as you tilt

name: Shoulder blade squeeze
steps: Sit tall with your arms loose by your sides.
Gently draw your shoulder blades back and together, as if holding a pencil between them.
Squeeze for a slow count of 2 while you breathe out, then let go.
stopIf: Tingling, numbness or pain that shoots down an arm or leg

name: Ankle alphabet
tl: Isulat ang ABC gamit ang paa
steps: Sit back in a chair and lift one foot off the floor.
Use your big toe like a pen and draw the letters of the alphabet in the air. Small and slow is fine.
Rest your foot, then do the other foot.
stopIf: Your calf cramps and does not ease
A swollen, hot or red calf. Tell your doctor

name: Seated knee straighten and hold
steps: Sit at the front of a chair with your back tall.
Slowly straighten one knee until your leg is level. Keep your breathing easy.
Lower it with control. Do all on one leg, then the other.

name: Seated gentle twist
steps: Sit tall near the front of the chair, feet flat.
Cross your arms over your chest, or hold the chair back with one hand.
Turn your chest slowly to the right as far as is comfortable, breathing out as you turn.
Come back to the middle and turn to the left. Do not force it.
stopIf: Pain in your back that gets worse as you turn

video.title: Deskercise - Lower Back and Torso Stretches

name: Seated back arch and rounding
steps: Sit tall with your hands on your knees.
Breathe in and gently lift your chest, easing your back into a small arch.
Breathe out and let your back round softly, chin tucked a little.
Keep both movements small and slow.
stopIf: Tingling, numbness or pain that shoots down an arm or leg

name: Lying knee rolls
steps: Lie on your back on a firm bed or mat with knees bent, feet flat.
Keeping your shoulders down, slowly let both knees fall gently to the right.
Bring them back to the middle, then let them fall to the left.
Go only as far as feels easy.

name: Pelvic tilt
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, arms by your sides.
Breathe out and gently flatten the small of your back onto the bed or mat.
Hold for 2 counts while breathing normally, then relax.
stopIf: Back pain that shoots into your leg

name: Seated knee out to the side
steps: Sit tall near the front of the chair.
Slowly open one knee out to the side like opening a book, keeping your foot on the floor.
Bring it back to the middle, then do the other knee.
stopIf: Pinching pain deep in the hip

name: Standing leg back, holding a chair
steps: Stand behind a sturdy chair or counter and hold it with both hands.
Slowly lift one leg straight back without bending your knee or leaning forward.
Lower it slowly and switch legs.
stopIf: You feel unsteady and have nothing to hold

video.title: Back Leg Raise Strength Exercise for Older Adults

name: Slow sway (tai chi style)
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, one hand on a chair or counter.
Slowly shift your weight to the right foot, then to the left, like a gentle sway.
Let your arms float. Breathe slowly and keep your knees soft.
stopIf: You feel unsteady and have nothing to hold

video.title: Mayo Clinic Minute: Tai chi keeps seniors on their feet

name: Side steps along the counter
steps: Stand sideways beside a kitchen counter, one hand resting on it.
Step your feet to the side, one at a time, toward the end of the counter.
Step back the other way. Keep your toes pointing forward.
stopIf: You feel unsteady and have nothing to hold

name: Feet together stand
steps: Stand beside a counter with your fingertips on it.
Bring your feet together and stand tall. Breathe normally.
Try for 10 seconds, then rest. Work up slowly.
stopIf: You feel unsteady and have nothing to hold

name: Clock reach
steps: Stand beside a sturdy chair, one hand on the back of it.
Imagine a clock in front of you. Slowly reach your free arm to 12, then 3, with your knees soft.
Return to the middle, then switch hands.
stopIf: You feel unsteady and have nothing to hold

name: Chair dip
steps: Sit in a sturdy chair that cannot slide, hands on the seat beside your hips.
Lean forward a little, then press into your hands to lift your hips off the seat slightly.
Lower slowly, breathing out as you lift.

video.title: Chair Dip Strength Exercise for Older Adults

name: Seated overhead press
steps: Sit tall holding a light water bottle in each hand at shoulder height.
Breathe out and lift both arms overhead until they are almost straight.
Lower slowly while breathing in.

video.title: Overhead Arm Raise Strength Exercise for Older Adults

name: Thigh squeeze
steps: Sit tall with your leg out straight on a footstool or the floor.
Tighten the muscle on top of your thigh and press the back of the knee down. Count to 3 slowly.
Relax fully. Switch legs.

name: Leg raise to the front, holding a chair
steps: Stand holding a sturdy chair or counter with both hands.
Slowly lift one knee in front of you to a comfortable height.
Lower it with control. Do all on one side, then the other.
stopIf: You feel unsteady and have nothing to hold

name: Sideways leg lift, holding a chair
steps: Stand tall holding a chair or counter. Keep your toes pointing forward.
Slowly lift one leg out to the side, keeping your body upright.
Lower it slowly. Switch legs.
stopIf: You feel unsteady and have nothing to hold

name: Seated heel pull-back
steps: Sit tall at the front of a chair.
Slide one foot back under the chair, then press the toes down and squeeze the back of the thigh.
Slide it back out. Do all on one side, then the other.
stopIf: Your thigh cramps and does not ease

name: Shoulder and arm stretch
steps: Sit tall. Bring your right arm across your chest.
Use your left hand to hold it gently at the elbow. Hold the stretch for a slow breath out.
Let go and switch arms. Do not pull hard.
stopIf: Tingling, numbness or pain that shoots down an arm or leg

video.title: Shoulder and Arm Stretch for Older Adults

name: Single knee hug
steps: Lie on your back on a firm bed or mat with knees bent.
Use both hands behind one thigh to draw it gently toward your chest.
Hold for a slow breath out, then lower the foot and switch legs.
stopIf: Pain in the hip or knee

name: Seated hip stretch
steps: Sit tall at the front of a sturdy chair.
Rest your right ankle across your left knee, keeping the right foot flexed.
Sit tall and breathe slowly. You should feel a stretch in the outer hip only.
Hold for 15 to 20 seconds, then switch sides.
stopIf: You cannot do it without leaning over

name: Breathing walk
steps: Walk at an easy pace on level ground, or up and down a hallway.
Breathe in through your nose for 3 steps.
Breathe out slowly for 4 steps, lips a little pursed.
Keep that rhythm. Slow down if you cannot count it comfortably.
stopIf: You are short of breath and it does not settle

name: Slow mindful walk
steps: Walk slowly in a safe, clear space, indoors or in the garden.
Feel each heel land, then the whole foot, then your toes.
Let your breath be easy. Notice three things you can see or hear.

name: Pursed-lip walk
tl: Lakad na may pursed-lip na paghinga
steps: Stand tall, then start walking slowly.
Breathe in through your nose for 2 steps.
Breathe out through pursed lips, as if blowing out a candle, for 4 steps.
Rest on a chair any time you need it.
stopIf: You are short of breath and it does not settle
Your lips or fingertips look blue
